title: Choosing lead sources and the four-stage offer chain
audience: Owners deciding where new enquiries come from and how an enquiry becomes a regular client
learningOutcomes: Rank lead sources by enquiries produced per hour of effort, using the learner's own figures
Describe the four stages of the offer chain and the job each stage does
Find the largest drop-off in a funnel and choose one change to test

instruction.heading: Rank channels by return on effort
instruction.body: Lead sources differ in how quickly they start a conversation and how much effort they take. Personal contact, calls to people who already know you, and referrals often produce enquiries faster than broad public advertising, but each business should confirm this from its own numbers. Compare channels on one measure: enquiries produced per hour of effort over a set period, such as 30 days. Record the counts rather than relying on how a channel feels.

instruction.heading: Four stages of the offer chain
instruction.body: The lead source brings a prospect in. The entry offer is a low-commitment first step, such as a trial session, a free assessment or a short introductory block. The core offer is the main ongoing service most clients buy. The back-end offer is a further programme or product for clients who are already satisfied. Each stage needs deliberate design, because a weak stage drags down the ones after it.

instruction.heading: Find the bottleneck, then change one thing
instruction.body: Count prospects at each stage over the same period. The stage with the largest percentage drop-off is the bottleneck. Improving a stage that already converts well rarely changes income much. Fix one thing at the bottleneck, test it for 30 days, and count again. Adding leads does not repair a broken step; it only sends more people through the same leak.

procedure: List every channel used in the last 30 days and the hours spent on each.
Divide the enquiries from each channel by its hours to get enquiries per hour.
Write the four stages across a page and enter the counts for the same period.
Circle the stage with the largest percentage drop-off.
Choose one change at that stage and set a 30-day review date.

workedExamples.situation: A hypothetical studio records 40 enquiries, 24 trial sessions and 4 new members in one month.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Where is the bottleneck, and what is the first action?
workedExamples.reasoning: Only 4 of 24 trial attendees join, so the largest loss sits between the trial and the first paid plan. The first action is to review the trial experience and the offer that follows, not to buy more leads. More leads would add people to the same step. Re-measure after 30 days.

equipmentAndPpe: Time log for hours per channel

commonErrors.error: Ranking channels by how fashionable they feel
commonErrors.prevention: Rank by enquiries per hour from recorded counts.

commonErrors.error: Buying more leads when conversion is the real problem
commonErrors.prevention: Find the bottleneck stage before spending on lead sources.

commonErrors.error: Treating the entry offer as the product itself
commonErrors.prevention: Each stage has a job; the core offer is the service the business exists to deliver.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Check each platform's policy and ACCC advertising guidance for fitness or massage services before spending.
Electronic contact with prospects is subject to the Spam Act 2003. See the contact lesson before using any electronic channel.

qualityStandard: Each channel has enquiries per hour recorded for the same period
The bottleneck is identified from counts
One change is tested with a review date set
documentationEvidence: Channel table with hours and enquiries
Four-stage funnel with counts and review date
summary: Rank channels by enquiries per hour of effort.
Four stages: lead, front-end, core, back-end.
Fix the largest drop-off before buying more leads.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which measure does this lesson recommend for comparing lead sources?
options: How fashionable the channel feels to the owner and staff
Enquiries produced per hour of effort over a set period
The largest audience a channel reaches in the whole area

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the entry offer?
options: The lowest-commitment first step that brings a prospect into the business
The most detailed programme on the menu, booked first at full price
The final product for loyal clients and the most expensive one on the menu

knowledgeChecks.question: The largest drop-off is between the trial and the first paid plan. What is the sensible first action?
options: Buy more lead sources and pay for more ads each month
Review the trial experience and the offer that follows
Cut the trial price to zero and give the trial away for free

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam
officialReferences.covers: Read via summary tool: marketing messages need the recipient's consent (express consent is the best practice; inferred consent is less reliable); each message must identify the sender accurately; each commercial message must include a free, working unsubscribe facility that is honoured within 5 working days. Publisher: Australian Communications and Media Authority. The Spam Act 2003 text itself was not read in this pass.

officialReferences.title: Advertising and selling guide: A guide for business
officialReferences.covers: Read via summary tool (first 100,000 of about 123,600 characters): businesses must not mislead or deceive in advertising, including online and social media content, and the test is the overall impression created. On pricing, the guide says to state the total price, including mandatory fees and taxes, before the customer agrees. The guide does not address quotes or estimates directly. Publisher: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission. Platform-specific rules remain UNCONFIRMED.
